related_questions.question: What is the drug of choice for Duchenne muscular dystrophy?
related_questions.snippet: Corticosteroids, such as prednisone, deflazacort, and vamoralone, are commonly prescribed to people with DMD to slow the progression of muscle weakness and delay the loss of ambulation (walking ability). Long-term side effects include weight gain, behavioral changes, growth suppression, bone loss, and cataracts.

text_blocks.snippet: Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD) currently has no cure, but several medications and therapies are used to manage symptoms and potentially slow disease progression. These include corticosteroids like prednisone and deflazacort, which can help maintain muscle strength and function. Additionally, gene therapies like Elevidys (delandistrogene moxeparvovec-rokl) and exon-skipping medications like casimersen (AMONDYS 45), eteplirsen (Exondys 51), golodirsen (Vyondys 53), and viltolarsen (Viltepso) are available for specific genetic mutations. Givinostat (Duvyzat) is a nonsteroidal medication that has also been approved to treat DMD.

list.title: Corticosteroids (Prednisone, Deflazacort):
list.snippet: These medications help reduce inflammation, maintain muscle strength, and potentially prolong ambulation. Deflazacort (Emflaza) is an FDA-approved option for DMD patients aged 2 and older.

list.title: Gene Therapy (Elevidys):
list.snippet: Elevidys is the first gene therapy approved for DMD, specifically for patients with a confirmed mutation in the DMD gene.

list.title: Exon-Skipping Medications:
list.snippet: These medications, such as casimersen, eteplirsen, golodirsen, and viltolarsen, target specific genetic mutations and help the body produce a shorter, functional dystrophin protein.

list.title: Givinostat (Duvyzat):
list.snippet: This nonsteroidal medication is an HDAC inhibitor that helps reduce inflammation and loss of muscle. It's approved for DMD patients six years and older who can still walk.

list.title: Other Supportive Therapies:
list.snippet: These include physical therapy, respiratory care, and cardiac care, which are crucial for managing DMD symptoms and improving quality of life.
